title: UGC-NET / CSIR-NET
kicker: National Eligibility Test for lectureship, JRF and PhD

value.body: National tests run by NTA, held twice a year (usually June and December). UGC-NET covers humanities, social sciences, commerce, management, computer science and other subjects; the Joint CSIR-UGC NET covers five science areas — chemical, earth, life, mathematical and physical sciences. A qualifying score makes you eligible for Assistant Professor posts, PhD admission, or a Junior Research Fellowship (JRF).

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A master's degree with at least 55% (50% for SC/ST/OBC-NCL/PwD and some other groups), or a final-year master's student; a four-year bachelor's degree with 75% is also accepted under current rules. Register with NTA for the June or December cycle and choose your subject. JRF has an upper age limit; Assistant Professor and PhD-only eligibility do not.

value.title: At a glance
items: Since 2024, results come in three tiers: JRF + Assistant Professor, Assistant Professor + PhD admission, and PhD admission only.
JRF is very competitive: only a small share of candidates qualify for it in each cycle.
Qualifying NET makes you eligible for teaching posts — actual hiring is through separate college and university recruitment.
The JRF award is valid for a limited period, so it is usually linked to joining a PhD soon after.

value.title: UGC-NET June 2025: who qualified for what
value.note: About 7.5 lakh candidates appeared in this cycle.
